name: Worth the Trip
tagline: You always make them laugh at the wrong moment. It's always the right one.
epigraph: The story goes that the drink behind this one reached the front by taxi.
language_row: Wren's Resonance (v6): ready. Sibling echoes moved off: *A Brother's Care*'s "this drink's ancestor" (epigraph), the Craftsman's "what you rarely say out loud", creator-lover's "you watch their face", creator-outlaw's "you keep to yourself", creator-hero's "the soda goes in" (y4 now "the fizz comes last, once you're there"); pronouns he/his all Joe Scialom (accepted by Wren). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/joe-scialom-suffering-bastard.md` (*Oxford Companion* SCIALOM pdf 1767, incl. Jeff Berry's account, labelled as his; *A Proper Drink* p. 264). Craft: *Flavor Matrix* pdf 132 (cooked ginger: gingerol to zingerone, "less spice and a strong pine aroma"; cumin as ginger's pairing), pdf 135 (Ginger Mule syrup, adapted); *Cocktail Codex* p. 22 (split base), p. 48 (syrup and soda for ginger beer), pp. 139–140 (Mule, "more a Highball than a sour"). Set aside: `fact-cards/hanky-panky.md` (Oxford HANKY PANKY pdf 966; the sibling *Quite Alive*'s story). Room notes: `work/caregiver-jester/`.
names_note: **Worth the Trip**, the room's pick (all three): showing up, the taxi without saying "taxi"; it credits the guest for coming. Also considered: *On My Way* (Wren: the text this person sends when it's bad; kept on the list for Robin), *Well Timed* (echoes the tagline), *Hang On* (leans on the "Hang in there" meme), *By Taxi* and *Four Gallons* (about the story, not the person).
open_items: **The swear word:** the drink behind this one is named once in the reading as the Suffering Bastard. Wren flags it for Robin; Hester's fence: who named it, and why, is not on record, so the reading says "I've never found out who named it" and signposts "I like to think".

**Family, a judgement call:** Tomás files it as Highball (the classic's spirit-plus-ginger-beer build, *Proper* p. 264; syrup and soda as ginger beer, *Codex* p. 48); the *Codex* puts lime-and-ginger-syrup long drinks in the Daiquiri chapter (pp. 139–140). Argued in Checks for Robin to overrule.
**Not veto-free:** ginger carries the spice veto (added to the table on the safe side). First Caregiver pour that isn't veto-free; the floor holds (12 of 15 in the registry).
**Cumin strength (unsourced):** doubled to 1 tsp per ~560 ml syrup (~0.1 g a drink) so it is tasted; how strongly it comes through is Tomás's judgement, marked unsourced in Checks.
**Contested date:** 1942 appears only inside Berry's attribution; *A Proper Drink* says "the late '40s". The regulars' rank isn't given ("his regulars from the Eighth Army").

**Ours, never his:** neither printed recipe is the original (Oxford: shaken, Collins, 15 ml cordial; *Proper*: stirred, rocks, 30 ml). The reading says "The gin and brandy together are his. The rest is mine."

**Runners-up:** the Penicillin (Sam Ross, 2005; *Proper* pp. 170–171; name origin not on the page); the Corpse Reviver as a transatlantic joke (Oxford pdf 584); the Hanky Panky (set aside: the sibling *Quite Alive*'s story).
